answer: Every agent identity must hold a scarce stake burned on misbehaviour. An oracle pairs each agent with a ferrous token seeded at manufacture, so cloning a key means re-fabricating silicon, not copying a file. Each identity also locks a deposit, and the protocol issues a pulse each epoch only real hardware can sign. Forging ten thousand agents costs ten thousand chips plus as many deposits, and one failed attestation burns the stake. Cost scales linearly with identity count while payoff per identity does not, so fakes never pay; honest operators wander between tasks on one durable identity.
